Work started late today so I stayed up late last night, planning to sleep in. Every other day this week I had to wake up early and would hit snooze 3-4 times and fall asleep. However, today I woke up at the same time with no alarm and couldn't get back to sleep for an hour. This has happened quite a few times and I was wondering if there is a scientific reason behind this. Thanks!
Why is it when I wake up early because I have to I want to get back to sleep (and often do) but when I wake up early and can sleep in I can't get back to sleep?
I too would like an explanation on this

Well I'm no expert but it seems you can't go back to sleep when your body naturally wakes up. There's something signaling your body that it's time to wake up so you'll have a hard time going back to sleep when your body is telling you to wake up. When you wake up with an alarm clock your body is still telling you to go back to sleep because it's tired. That's my guess.

If you wake up on your own, your body does it naturally at the time that is most convenient for your brain. When you wake up with an alarm, your brain wasn't prepared for that and was probably in the middle of doing something. When you sleep, your brain organizes all the information you leaned throughout the day. Think of waking up naturally like waking up with everything in one place and ready to go, and waking up with an alarm like waking up with everything out of place and unorganized. Obviously your brain is going to tell you you need to go back to sleep so it can fix this mess.
